2. Resources, connections and symbols

David Sarrat González

Source: vignettes/book-02-connect.Rmd
book-02-connect.Rmd

What you will learn

Distinguish a connection, a resource and a symbol, and change databases deliberately.

You need: the packages, helpers and loaded practice data from Getting started. Start a fresh R session in book-work and run the sections in order.

Start this chapter 

library(dsOMOPClient)
source("tools/book/display.R")
source("tools/book/connection.R")
practice <- book_connect("gibleed")
conns <- practice$conns

Three names with different jobs

A connection is a logged-in DataSHIELD session. A resource describes how the server opens a database. A symbol is an object name in that session. Here site names the connection, gibleed selects the resource and omop names the attached database handle.

DSI::datashield.symbols(conns)
#> $site
#> [1] "omop"

Under site, omop is the private handle created by book_connect(). Later, D_people will name a table created by a recipe, rather than a database handle.

For an Opal study server, use the login block in Getting started. Your administrator provides resource names including their project prefix.

Use a handle explicitly 

knitr::kable(as.data.frame(ds.omop.table.stats("person", symbol = "omop", conns = conns)$per_site$site))
rows persons
2690 2690

The request goes to GiBleed through omop: its person count is in the 2,690–2,694 band. Most dsOMOP calls default to symbol = "omop", so you can omit it when you have just one attached database. ds.omop.server.version() is different: it reports the server’s installed and available methods, independently of any database handle.

Switch resources

The practice helper closes the current session and opens the requested resource. Always replace conns with the returned connection:

practice <- book_switch("numeric")
conns <- practice$conns
knitr::kable(as.data.frame(ds.omop.table.stats("person", conns = conns)$per_site$site))
rows persons
25 25

The person band is now 25–29, containing Synthea27Nj’s 28 people. The handle can still be called omop even though its database changed. Switching does not combine the two populations. On Opal, use the disconnect/attach pair in Getting started instead.

practice <- book_switch("gibleed")
conns <- practice$conns
knitr::kable(as.data.frame(ds.omop.table.stats("person", conns = conns)$per_site$site))
rows persons
2690 2690

The 2,690–2,694 band confirms that GiBleed is attached again. Choosing the resource explicitly prevents running a lab analysis against its empty numeric fields.

Exercise 1: keep two handles in one session

Attach the numeric resource as labs, keeping omop attached to GiBleed. List the names and count people through each. Does attaching labs combine them? For Opal, substitute the supplied numeric resource name.

Solution

labs_session <- ds.omop.connect(resource = "numeric", symbol = "labs", conns = conns)
DSI::datashield.symbols(conns)
#> $site
#> [1] "labs" "omop"

labs and omop are two distinct handles in the same session.

handle_counts <- lapply(c("omop", "labs"), function(handle) {
  counts <- ds.omop.table.stats("person", stats = "persons",
    symbol = handle, conns = conns)$per_site$site
  data.frame(Handle = handle, counts)
})
knitr::kable(do.call(rbind, handle_counts), row.names = FALSE)
Handle persons
omop 2690
labs 25 
ds.omop.disconnect(symbol = "labs", conns = conns)

omop gives 2690 and labs gives 25. Each is a separate protected count; the populations were not combined. Disconnecting labs leaves omop available.

Exercise 2: diagnose a wrong name

Ask for a person count through missing_handle. What needs fixing: the table name or the handle name?

Solution

tryCatch(ds.omop.table.stats("person", symbol = "missing_handle", conns = conns),
  error = function(e) cat(conditionMessage(e), "\n"))
#> No OMOP session 'missing_handle'. Call ds.omop.connect() first.

The message identifies a missing session handle. It says nothing about whether the database has a person table. Use omop, or attach a resource under the name you intend to query.

End the session 

ds.omop.disconnect(conns = conns)
DSI::datashield.logout(conns)

Disconnect releases the database handle; logout ends the DataSHIELD session. The next chapter opens a fresh connection.

Recap

A resource selects a database, a connection carries requests, and a symbol names a private server object. Check the selected resource before analysing it.
